title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: Estimation probability distributions available 'distionary' package. Wraps 'lmom' package fitting L-moments, 'ismev' package fitting GP/GEV/Gumbel MLE, 'fitdistrplus' package combinations.

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
code: fit_dst(   family,   x,   method = c("mle", "mge", "mme", "lmom", "lmom-log"),   na_action = c("null", "drop", "fail"),   on_unres = c("null", "fail") )

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: family Name target distribution family, "norm", "gev", "pois". See details. Character vector length 1. x Numeric vector containing observations fit. method Estimation method use. Valid choices include "mle", "mge", "mme", "lmom", "lmom-log". default "mle". na_action Strategy dealing NA values x. "null" returns Null distribution (distionary::dst_null()); "drop" silently removes missing observations fitting; "fail" aborts error. on_unres Behaviour distribution can resolved supplied inputs. "null" (default) yields Null distribution (distionary::dst_null()) distribution warning, whereas "fail" propagates error.

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: distribution object class "dst" encapsulating fitted distribution.

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: fit_dst() function currently lightweight fitting wrapper, pre-specified behaviour certain family / method combinations. full list families compatible estimation methods available via specific family wrappers, fit_dst_norm(), fit_dst_pois(), etc. fitting implemented. method = "lmom" distribution families 'gamma', 'gev', 'gp', 'gumbel', 'lnorm', 'norm', 'pearson3', 'weibull', 'lmom' package wrapped first calling lmom::samlmu() data vector x calculate L-moments, relevant lmom::pel*() function called estimate parameters. method = "lmom" distribution families 'exp', 'pois', 'bern', 'geom', 'chisq', 'unif', method L-moments manually implemented. families except 'unif' single parameter mean needed (thus equivalent 'mme' method). 'unif' family minimum maximum parameter values calculated l1 - 3 * l2  l1 + 3 * l2, l1 l2 first second L-moments. method = "lmom-log", 'lnorm' 'lp3' families supported, otherwise distribution resolved. method fits distributions via 'lmom' method log scale. , 'norm' 'pearson3' distributions fit log data, respective 'lnorm' 'lp3' distribution obtained. method = "mle" distribution families 'gev', 'gp', 'gumbel', 'ismev' package used fit distribution maximum likelihood estimation. done invoking functions ismev::gev.fit(), ismev::gpd.fit() (threshold = 0), ismev::gum.fit() (respectively). method = "mle" distribution family 'bern' 'degenerate', MLE calculated manually. 'bern', parameter estimated mean 0-1 data; 'degenerate', unique data value. families 'empirical' 'finite', empirical distribution fit supplied data. 'null' family, Null distribution returned. combination family method, fitdistrplus::fitdist() function called inserting data x, family name, method. distributions require starting values parameters. families 't', 'pearson3', 'f', 'chisq', done moment matching ('mme'), 'lp3', log. 'gev', 'gp', 'gumbel', MLE used starting values (method = "mle"). understand distribution families , see documentation 'distionary' package dst_*() functions. example, 'lp3' family can found ?distionary::dst_lp3(). Note Gumbel distribution available yet 'distionary', simply 'gev' family shape = 0. understand estimation methods, see 'lmom' package "lmom" method. "lmom-log" method, "lmom", via log data corresponding log-transformed distributions. others, see 'fitdistrplus' package documentation.

what: Handling of missing or unresolvable data
title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
text: na_action = "drop", function operates subset x without missing values (via x <- x[!.na(x)]). takes priority behaviour indicated on_unres. fitting fails, Null distribution output on_unres = "null" (default), error thrown on_unres = "fail". Fitting can fail due enough data, able isolate single distribution, various reasons typically otherwise result error NA parameters wrapped fitting method.

title: Fit a distribution — fit_dst
code: fit_dst("norm", x = 1:10, method = "mle") #> Loading required namespace: testthat #> Normal distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>     mean       sd  #> 5.500000 2.872281  fit_dst("gev", x = c(1, 4, 3, NA, 5), method = "lmom", na_action = "drop") #> Generalised Extreme Value distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>   location      scale      shape  #>  3.0145621  2.1806961 -0.7498928  fit_dst("pois", x = c(1, 4, 3, NA, 5), na_action = "null") #> Null distribution (NA)   # "lnorm" with "lmom-log" shares parameters with "norm" fit by "lmom". fit_dst("lnorm", x = 1:10, method = "lmom-log") #> Log Normal distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>   meanlog     sdlog  #> 1.5104413 0.7487066  fit_dst("norm", x = log(1:10), method = "lmom") #> Normal distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>      mean        sd  #> 1.5104413 0.7487066

title: Fit Distributions by Family — fit_dst_family_wrappers
code: # Calls can be quite simple. fit_dst_norm(1:10) #> Normal distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>     mean       sd  #> 5.500000 2.872281  fit_dst_gumbel(2:6) #> Generalised Extreme Value distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #> location    scale    shape  #> 3.296709 1.266557 0.000000   # Still have access to the functionality available through `fit_dst()` x <- c(1, 4, 3, NA, 5) fit_dst_lnorm(x, method = "lmom", na_action = "null") #> Null distribution (NA)  fit_dst_lnorm(x, method = "lmom", na_action = "drop") #> Log Normal distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>   meanlog     sdlog  #> 0.9931290 0.6091404   # Fitting by l-moments on the log-scale not the same as original scale. fit_dst_lnorm(x, method = "lmom-log", na_action = "drop") #> Log Normal distribution (continuous)  #> --Parameters-- #>   meanlog     sdlog  #> 1.0235861 0.7556555

title: Rank-based Scores — uscore
text: Converts numeric vector rank-based scores. uscore() (uniform scores), values become roughly equally spaced 0 1, keeping order. nscore() calculates normal scores spacing uniform scores along standard normal distribution; rpscore() calculates empirical return periods spacing uniform scores u 1 / (1 - u).

title: Rank-based Scores — uscore
text: x Numeric vector. pos Positional adjustment uniform scores. See Details. Can single numeric, named one proponents behind choice numeric: "Weibull", "Beard", "Gringorten", "Hazen". na.rm Logical indicating whether NA NaN values removed output.

title: Rank-based Scores — uscore
text: Uniform scores calculated (rank+)/(n+1+2*), rank ranked x values, positional adjustment pos. Alternatively, named individual associated choice : Weibull (1939) proposed = 0. Beard (1943) proposed = -0.31. Gringorten (1963) proposed = -0.44. Hazen (1914) proposed = -0.5.
